raw_record.support_text: OXP-treated mice had extensive tumors throughout the liver; at the 74-week necropsy mean liver-to-body weight ratio of OXP-treated mice was 18.4% ± 8.9% vs 3.8% ± 0.3% in same-age controls, prompting early euthanasia of the 78-week group due to extensive tumors throughout the mice.
raw_record.extra_details: OXP-treated mice bore extensive liver tumors; histopathologic evaluation indicated few liver specimens were truly normal. OXP did not produce a measurable increase in mutant frequency (MF) in either liver or lung, with or without clonal correction after 74 or 78 weeks of treatment. Nontumor liver samples showed angiectasis, cytomegaly, and leukocytosis.

raw_record.support_text: In one bioassay, 36 rats were fed corn contaminated with 15-250 ppb AFB1 for 2 years (accumulated intake of 1.17-1.32 mg AFB1 per rat); 24 of them developed primary liver cancer (PLC), a carcinogenic rate of 66.7%.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Corn contaminated with 15-250 ppb AFB1 fed for 2 years with accumulated intake of 1.17-1.32 mg AFB1 per rat.
raw_record.extra_details: 24 of 36 rats (66.7%) developed PLC; result cited as reference [15].
